messages:
sara: Customer (tenant_42) opened a ticket: sporadic 429s on /v1/embeddings (model=embed-large-v2). They said it began immediately after a billing reconciliation at ~10:28 PDT. Sharing minimal logs and their curl repro.

sara: ```
[2026-03-12T17:28:12Z] tenant=tenant_42 key=APIKEY_ABC route=/v1/embeddings model=embed-large-v2 status=200 latency_ms=115
[2026-03-12T17:29:00Z] tenant=tenant_42 key=APIKEY_ABC route=/v1/embeddings model=embed-large-v2 status=429 reason=rate_limit remaining=0 window=60s
[2026-03-12T17:29:00Z] tenant=tenant_42 key=APIKEY_DEF route=/v1/embeddings model=embed-large-v2 status=429 reason=rate_limit remaining=0 window=60s
[2026-03-12T17:30:05Z] tenant=tenant_42 key=APIKEY_ABC route=/v1/embeddings model=embed-large-v2 status=429 reason=burst_exhausted remaining=0
```

sara: repro they gave (redacted key):

sara: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"embed-large-v2\",\"input\":[\"p1\",\"p2\",\"p3\"]}'
```

tony: looking. Did they run a retry/replay job after billing was fixed? Those often cause a sudden burst.

julia: FYI embed-large-v2 internal cost ~1200 token-equivalent per batch due to batching heuristics. A few concurrent workers will eat burst quota fast.

kevin: Can you run a quick aggregation for 429s by api_key in the incident window?

kevin: ```sql
SELECT api_key, COUNT(*) AS throttles, MIN(ts) AS first_seen, MAX(ts) AS last_seen
FROM request_logs
WHERE tenant='tenant_42' AND status=429 AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-12T17:20:00Z' AND '2026-03-12T17:40:00Z'
GROUP BY api_key
ORDER BY throttles DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

sara: Ran it  top offenders: APIKEY_ABC = 1,820 throttles, APIKEY_DEF = 420. ~81% of 429s from APIKEY_ABC concentrated 17:29:00-17:31:30Z.

datadog-bot: Alert: support.quota.throttle.count (tenant:tenant_42) > 75 in 5m at 2026-03-12T17:29:00Z. Link: https://datadog.example/graph/xyz

tony: pattern matches a single client flood (likely a bulk retry). Immediate mitigations we can do:
- advise customer to add jitter and client-side rate limiting for the replay job
- suggest smaller page sizes / incremental batches
- temporarily bump tenant burst allowance while they drain the queue (requires billing confirmation)

kevin: For observability and paging alerts I propose adding:
- Datadog monitor scoped to tenant + route + status:429 by api_key (alert if any key > X in 5m)
- Console panels: per-tenant 429 rate, top api_keys by throttle count, burst_token_balance timeline, model heatmap by RPM

kevin: example monitor query (Datadog):

kevin: "avg(last_5m):sum:requests{tenant:tenant_42,route:/v1/embeddings,status:429} by {api_key} > 5"

sara: I enabled higher-sample capture for tenant_42 for 45 minutes and created a temporary tenant dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/t42/embeddings-spike (sampling on).

datadog-bot: Sampling enabled for tenant_42 body_capture=on duration=45m by sara

tony: Action plan:
1) Support (sara) advise customer to pause/retry with jitter and reduce per-request batch size.
2) SRE (tony) will increase tenant_42 burst bucket by +40% for 2 hours and keep watch.
3) DevEx (kevin) will add the Datadog monitor + dashboard panels and link runbook.
4) Eng-ML (julia) to evaluate an on-429 fallback to embed-small-v1 for this route as a traffic-shedding strategy.

tony: I applied the +40% burst bump at 2026-03-12T17:35:00Z. Rolling monitor; will auto-revert at 19:05 PDT unless extended.

kevin: Monitor created: tenant_429_spike_t42 -> notify #support-oncall, #eng-runtime. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/ops/tenant-429-playbook

sara: Customer confirmed the bulk job finished cleanly after we bumped the burst bucket and they throttled retries. No further 429s reported. They're going to stagger the job going forward.

julia: Follow-up ticket: detect single-key flood patterns and surface a "throttle-warning" header + optional auto-fallback to cheaper embedding model. Filing to ENG-ML backlog.

sara: Closing this thread; will add a short post-incident note in support with dashboard links and the SQL query used. :thumbsup:
